summary: Jonathan Lear is a philosopher who studied at Yale University (~1965–1969), the University of Cambridge (~1970–1973), and The Rockefeller University (~1973–1978). He held a post at the University of Chicago from around 1996 to 2025.

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer specializes in indology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (~1970–1983), and became a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford College, Yale Divinity School, and Yale University. He held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1966–1968) and the University of Chicago (~1968–2013).

Jong-Nam Choi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Shitennoji University and the University of Hamburg (PhD 1998). His teachers included doctoral supervisor Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is a Buddhist studies and indology scholar educated at Seoul National University and the University of Tokyo (PhD 1994, under Yasunori Ejima). He held positions at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2001).

Jongmyung Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA (MA 1994). He served as an Associate Professor at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).
Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Ryukoku University, where he later served as a professor from around 1964 to 1987.
Josef Schick was an indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He held academic posts at Heidelberg University (~1890–1896) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1896–1926).

Joseph Campbell was a religious studies scholar who studied at Canterbury School, Dartmouth, Columbia, the University of Paris, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich. He taught at Canterbury School (1933–1934) and Sarah Lawrence College (1934–1972).
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed a Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was a scholar of indology and history/archaeology who studied at Brooklyn College (~1945–1949). He served as Professor Emeritus of geography at the University of Minnesota, where he held a post from around 1964 to 2000.
Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Columbia University (~1961–1965). He also studied under Anagarika Munindra (~1967–1974) and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Joseph Hackin worked in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated in Paris under Sylvain Lévi and others, he held posts at the Musée Guimet (1913–1941), the French Archeological Delegation to Afghanistan, and the EPHE.

Joseph John Loizzo is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Amherst, Harvard, and under Robert A. F. Thurman. He founded the Nalanda Institute and served as a Visiting Scholar of Religion at Columbia University (attested 2007).
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who studied at Columbia University from around 1946 to 1953. He held a long-term academic post at Temple University from around 1968 to 2021.

Joseph Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017), where he studied under his doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and under Collett Cox.

Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa was a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Rikkyo University and the University of Chicago (PhD 1951). He served on the University of Chicago faculty (~1951–1985), including as Dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy and religious studies. He has been on the faculty at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and held visiting professorships at UCSB, United Theological College, Bangalore, and the Bossey Ecumenical Institute.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar of indology, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at INALCO (1838), the Société Asiatique (1852), and the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1854).
Joseph Walser is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.
